newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Renault employees to vote on resuming work.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Renault employees to vote on resuming work.

text.p: Workers at French carmaker Renault's condemned Belgian plant will vote on Thursday whether to end their five-week-old strike while they negotiate over their future.

"In the light of the fact that we face a long procedure, a procedure that will take months we have asked them to restart work, and this proposition will be voted on Thursday," union organiser Karel Gacoms told RTBF radio on Monday.

The workers have been occupying the factory since they were told unexpectedly on February 27 that their profitable plant at Vilvoorde near Brussels would be closed in July with the loss of 3,100 jobs.
In the process they have been holding billions of francs in finished cars to ransom.
"We will propose to the workers to continue occupying the factory," Gacoms said, indicating that the cars would remain in their hands as a bargaining chip.
The Vilvoorde workers, who clashed with riot police during a march through Brussels on Friday, have staged sporadic protests in Belgium and France with colleagues from France and Spain.

They won moral victories in Belgium on Thursday and France on Friday when courts ruled that Renault had broken the law on prior consultation with workers and therefore had to restart the closure process from scratch.
Renault, which last year lost 5.2 billion francs, has said it will appeal the rulings and that there is no alternative to closing Vilvoorde.
"We don't want a long term strike to the finish, a strike that will exhaust people. So we think it is necessary to resume work while continuing the occupation," Gacoms said.
